## Summary

**Question:** KO's lead over PiS in the last IBRiS/Rzeczpospolita poll published before Aug 8, 2026.

**Key finding:** The question author's premise was factually wrong. The author stated the late-July reading was KO 30.1% vs PiS 28.7% (+1.4pp), but the actual latest IBRiS/Rzeczpospolita poll (fieldwork 24-25 July 2026) reports **KO 30.1% vs PiS 17.3% = +12.8pp**. PiS collapsed because Morawiecki's new "Rozwój Plus" party (7.4%) was split out following the PiS split. The 28.7% figure was a conflation with other pollsters (United Surveys ~28%, IPSOS ~28%).

**Critical resolution insight:** The ~21.5% "baseline" PiS figure exists only in the WP/United Surveys-by-IBRiS series, which the fine print **explicitly disregards**. The qualifying rp.pl series publishes only the 17.3% variant, so "headline as reported" = 17.3 → +12.8pp.

**Distribution:** Heavily concentrated at +12.8 (median 12.6), with a lower tail (P10 ~6.0) driven mainly by the ~28% chance a new IBRiS/Rz poll publishes before Aug 7. The open upper bound was essential — most probability mass sits at or above the author's stated +10 ceiling.

- **Median:** +12.6 pp
- **P10–P90:** +6.0 to +13.2 pp

The premortem gate caught and corrected an initial over-weighting of a resolver-invalid "baseline" fork, recentering the distribution appropriately before final submission.

resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the value of the Koalicja Obywatelska (KO) support figure minus the Prawo i Sprawiedliwość (PiS) support figure, in percentage points, in the most recent nationwide parliamentary voting-intention poll conducted by IBRiS on behalf of the newspaper Rzeczpospolita and published on or before August 7, 2026. A positive value means KO is ahead; a negative value means PiS is ahead. For example, if KO polls 30.1% and PiS polls 28.7%, the question resolves to 1.4; if KO polls 27% and PiS polls 29%, it resolves to -2. The relevant poll is the IBRiS/Rzeczpospolita national "gdyby wybory odbyły się w najbliższą niedzielę" (Sejm voting-intention) survey with the latest fieldwork dates among those published by August 7, 2026, as reported on rp.pl (https://www.rp.pl/polityka). If the rp.pl figures are unavailable, the corresponding IBRiS row on the Wikipedia page "Opinion polling for the next Polish parliamentary election" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_next_Polish_parliamentary_election) will be used.
fine_print: Only polls commissioned by Rzeczpospolita and conducted by IBRiS count; IBRiS polls for other commissioners and other pollsters' polls for Rzeczpospolita are disregarded. If two qualifying IBRiS/Rzeczpospolita polls share the same latest fieldwork dates, the one published later is used. Support figures are the headline party voting-intention percentages as reported. If no qualifying IBRiS/Rzeczpospolita voting-intention poll is published between June 1, 2026 and August 7, 2026, the question is annulled.

revision_history.reviewer_assessment:
**Verdict rationale: the tentative center (10.5) is meaningfully too low; it should be ~12.5.** The downside fork that drags the median down rests on a resolver interpretation the resolution criteria explicitly exclude.

**What I verified in the trace:**
- The core headline claim (Factor 1) is well-grounded. The rp.pl article (the primary/authoritative resolution source) reports the standard "gdyby wybory do Sejmu" Voting Intention table as **KO 30.1% / PiS 17.3% → +12.8pp**, corroborated by GazetaPrawna, dorzeczy.pl, and wp.pl. No hallucination; Factor 1's +2.0 logit is correct in sign.
- Factor 4 (author's +1.4pp premise is a factual error / conflation with United Surveys ~28) is also supported by the trace.
- Resolution criteria are PROVIDED and detailed; no recovery failure. The counterargument is a genuine alternative story (not a token gesture). Tool_audit narrative is broadly consistent with the metrics.

**The core error — Factor 2 / Monte Carlo overweight a resolver-invalid "baseline" fork:**
Factor 2 claims 17.3 is a "HYPOTHETICAL scenario" and that a resolver "treating the standard/baseline (Rozwój Plus reabsorbed) would record PiS ~23-25 → lead ~5-7," assigning it ~38% weight inside the no-new-poll branch. The trace directly contradicts the premise:
- The agent's own fetch_url result states: **"Only ONE variant is reported (WITH Rozwój Plus)... The content does not show PiS at 28.7% in any variant."** There is NO published baseline PiS figure in the rp.pl/Rzeczpospolita poll.
- The baseline variants (PiS ~21.5 without Morawiecki) exist ONLY in the WP/United Surveys-by-IBRiS series — a **different commissioner that the resolution fine print explicitly disregards.**
- The resolution criteria say to use "the headline party voting-intention percentages **as reported**" on rp.pl. As reported = 17.3. Rozwój Plus being listed as a separate party in the standard "gdyby wybory" poll does not make PiS's reported figure hypothetical; 17.3 is the headline. The Wikipedia backup would likewise log the poll's reported PiS figure (17.3), not an invented reabsorption.

Thus a resolver mechanically computes 30.1 − 17.3 = **+12.8**. The agent's own findings file even concedes: "rp.pl article ONLY presented the 17.3 scenario → strongly favors +12.8." Yet the Monte Carlo still puts ~38% of the no-new-poll mass on a ~6.3 baseline cluster, pulling the median from 12.8 down to 10.5 and setting P10 at 4.6.

**My independent estimate:** The only genuine uncertainty is whether a NEW IBRiS/Rz poll publishes before Aug 7 (~28% is reasonable — the 24-25 Jul poll was off-cycle/event-driven; next scheduled ~late Aug). Conditional on no new poll (~72%), the answer is essentially exactly 12.8. In the new-poll branch, the fractured right persists near-term, so a new poll most likely still shows an elevated lead (~9-11) with real spread. This yields a distribution heavily concentrated at 12.8 with a modest lower tail — roughly P10 ~7, P50 ~12.5, P90 ~13.2 — NOT a symmetric bimodal split with a cluster at 6. The agent is over-weighting a resolver-interpretation fork the criteria exclude and double-counting downside uncertainty already present in the new-poll branch.

**Recommendation:** Remove (or drastically down-weight to <10%) the "baseline reabsorption" fork, since no such figure is published in the qualifying series and the criteria disregard the commissioner that does publish it. Recenter the distribution to median ~12.5 with the bulk of mass at 12.8 and the lower tail driven almost entirely by the ~28% new-poll probability.
